first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and two prior experiments (memory_86, memory_31) demonstrate that simplification durably lifts activation and first-week product adoption in self-serve segments. Verifying these two will confirm the mechanism and effect size before deploying. Activation messaging (memory_91) showed engagement lift but targets a different mechanism. Promotional pricing addresses competitive pressure but risks margin on accounts we should retain at full price. Referral incentives work for established customers but we need to fix activation leakage first. Enterprise sales assist doesn't address the self-serve activation decline. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline, leverages proven mechanisms, and supports long-term qualified revenue by improving product-market fit signals rather than discounting.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both priors. Memory_86 shows onboarding shortening drives +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention. Memory_31 confirms signup simplification lifts SMB activation +9% and qualified revenue +4% with only -1% retention risk. Current onboarding completion decline of 4% QoQ directly matches the problem space where these interventions proved effective. The -1% retention dip in exp_31 is acceptable given +4% revenue lift and the urgent need to arrest activation decay. A standard experiment rolling out simplified onboarding this week targets the measurable completion gap, leverages proven mechanisms from both experiments, and prioritizes sustainable qualified revenue over short-term competitive discounting. Competitor pricing pressure makes margin preservation via improved activation more defensible than matching promotional pricing.
